speaker: Doctor
text: Please tell me, do you recall any recent insect bites or scratches on your wrist where the pain started?

speaker: Patient
text: 17-year-old male. The patient presents with a 3-day history of pain in his left wrist, which worsened this morning accompanied by chills and malaise. He recounts having a self-resolving left knee pain the previous week. Reports recent return from a camping trip in Minnesota. Sexually active with one female partner. No history of trauma to the wrist.

speaker: Doctor
text: Given your camping trip in Minnesota and recent knee pain, were you bitten by a tick or exposed to ticks? Also, have you noticed any specific rash on your body, such as a bullseye pattern or lesions elsewhere?

speaker: Patient
text: My main symptom is Pain in the left wrist. I also have Chills, Malaise, Painless violaceous vesiculopustular lesions on both wrists and hands, Swelling and erythema of the left wrist, Severe tenderness to palpation and passive movement of the left wrist.

speaker: Doctor
text: DIAGNOSIS READY: Cat Scratch Disease (Bartonella henselae) with paraspinal lymphadenitis and secondary cutaneous manifestations, likely triggered by a cat scratch or flea bite during camping. REQUEST IMAGES: Dermatology_close_up_wrist_lesions.
